stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M amid defense demand
stories.body: True Anomaly secured a $190 million Series C funding round, reflecting the growing importance of co-orbital security and space domain awareness in defense. The company's valuation now stands at $1.6 billion, with the Department of Defense increasingly pulling through contracts. Investors seem convinced that cash flow in space often trumps innovative ideas.
stories.soWhat: When defense contracts are the hottest ticket in town, innovation can take a backseat.

stories.head: Stoke Space banks $260M for reusable rockets
stories.body: Stoke Space has successfully raised $260 million in Series C funding to advance its fully-reusable medium-lift launch system. The investment aims to scale up manufacturing in preparation for its first orbital launch. As the competition heats up, the question remains whether Stoke can deliver on its promises without adding to the orbital junkyard.
stories.soWhat: In a crowded launch market, being 'fully reusable' might just be the new baseline.

stories.head: FY27 budget boosts space resilience by $1.4B
stories.body: The FY27 budget markup has allocated an additional $1.4 billion for space resilience initiatives, signaling a significant commitment to strengthening U.S. capabilities in the face of increasing threats. This funding is part of a broader recognition that space is integral to national security, not just a playground for tech enthusiasts. The military seems to be finally taking space as seriously as it takes its coffee.
stories.soWhat: More budget means more opportunities—but also more scrutiny on how that money is spent.

watchlist.title: SpaceX's next Starship test looms
watchlist.body: With its 13th test flight under its belt, all eyes are on SpaceX to see if it can finally nail down a reliable launch cadence.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN extension impacts market
watchlist.body: Palantir's $480 million extension on the TITAN program could influence other companies' bidding strategies in the ground station space.

watchlist.title: Anduril and L3Harris partnership unfolds
watchlist.body: The collaboration on a tactical SDA constellation could shift the dynamics of space-based defense systems in the Indo-Pacific.

watchlist.title: Hypersonic test delays continue
watchlist.body: With yet another hypersonic glide-vehicle test slipping, the implications for military readiness and budget allocation are becoming clearer.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
